_doc: THE ONE PIN of the Unison binary the sync engines ship (#1084). Cloud Drive's Unison engine is the stateful two-way folder-pair sync that sits next to rclone (cloud/API remotes) and rsync (one-way backup). The binary lives in Cloud-Lib-Rclone-Engine.apk beside librclone.so, as libunison.so, for the reason rclone-binary.json::_doc gives (API 29+ execs only what the installer extracted into nativeLibraryDir). build.gradle (FetchUnisonBinaries) downloads each ABI's tarball ONCE, refuses on a sha256 mismatch of the tarball AND of the extracted binary, and refuses a binary carrying PT_INTERP. Nothing is downloaded at runtime.
_doc_one_version: ONE exact Unison version and ONE OCaml build, the same on EVERY peer. Unison refuses a client and a server whose versions differ (and an archive written by another version is not trusted), so the phone, the desktop home-manager and every fleet host must run the same release. `version` and `ocaml` here are the single declaration; each peer in `peers` declares its own copy in its own repository and ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks/test/test-unison-pin.sh fails when any copy differs, when a peer file cannot be read, or when a peer is not listed. `ocaml` is what `unison -version` prints in brackets; the build workflow and the guard both read it.
_doc_arm64: Upstream publishes a static linux build for x86_64 only (an arm64 glibc build would carry PT_INTERP and cannot run under bionic). The arm64 binary is therefore built from the upstream source tag v{version} on Alpine (musl, fully static) by .github/workflows/build-unison-static.yml and published as an immutable release asset of this repository; the tarball's sha256 below pins it, and the workflow fails when the OCaml it finds is not `ocaml`.
_doc_transport: Unison reaches a peer over SSH on the WireGuard mesh by `<host>.app` names. An Android app has no ssh binary it may exec, so the engine opens the SSH session in-process (sshj, the library the mounts engine already ships), runs `unison -server` on the peer through it and bridges that channel to a loopback socket; the profile's second root is socket://127.0.0.1:<port>/<path>. Host keys are trusted on first use and refused when they change.
_doc_peers: Each peer file is {"version": "<unison version>", "ocaml": "<ocaml version>"} in its repository, read by its Nix module to pin the package it installs. The guard reads them from a sibling checkout ($UNISON_PEERS_ROOT/<repo>/<path>), else from the GitHub contents API with $GH_TOKEN/$GITHUB_TOKEN, and FAILS when neither answers: a peer it cannot read is a peer it cannot vouch for.
